search_log: Searched for "Stephen King IT novel point of view third person first person interludes Mike Hanlon" and related narrator/structure queries.
Opened the Course Hero whole-book study guide, which explicitly distinguishes third-person omniscient main narration from five first-person interludes.
Opened LitCharts' First Interlude analysis and The Washington Post's structural review to verify that Mike's interludes are sustained first-person sections.

Searched university and scholarly-repository results concerning IT's narrative structure; a Nottingham thesis result discussed the five-part/interlude structure, but its PDF could not be opened reliably enough to use as a second Tier A/B ALTERNATING source.
Opened Simon & Schuster's official book page; it verified the work and edition but provided no diagnostic excerpt or point-of-view description.
No second opened Tier A/B source independently supporting the exact ALTERNATING label was found, so component first-person evidence was not counted toward high confidence.
person_note: The quote sample independently exposes sustained third-person narration in several event passages but contains no diagnostic excerpt from Mike Hanlon's first-person interludes. Opened web evidence resolves the structure: the main story is third-person omniscient, while five recurring, substantial interludes consist of Mike's first-person historical notes. Those sections use different base persons and therefore require ALTERNATING rather than THIRD; dialogue, direct thought, generalized-you aphorisms, and the Turtle's speech remain local material. Confidence is medium because only one opened whole-book source explicitly supports ALTERNATING and the remaining sources establish only the first-person component; the required two Tier A/B exact-label sources for high confidence are absent.
